[00:00:00.964] Hello everyone, welcome back to this course on engineering chemistry. We will continue with module six on corrosion chemistry and in today's class we are going to study about corrosion control.
[00:00:14.308] We will look at another method of corrosion control and that is using corrosion inhibitors. There are two types of corrosion inhibitors, anodic corrosion inhibitors and cathodic corrosion inhibitors. So we are going to study about them.
[00:00:29.828] Let us understand what exactly are corrosion inhibitors. Now as the name suggests, they are substances which are going to inhibit the corrosion reaction.
[00:00:42.640] So, how would we exactly define them? They are chemical substances which are added in small quantities to the corrosive environment in order to decrease the rate of corrosion. So here, wherever we see this corrosive environment, we are aware of what is the corrosive.
[00:01:00.304] Environment and based on that, and also the nature of the metal, which is which needs to be protected, we are going to choose a corrosion inhibitor and use it, add it to the corrosive environment, and this should be added only in small quantities.
[00:01:19.748] Now because we know there are two different reactions which happen at dianode and cathode, so there would be different types of corrosion inhibitors. So what exactly are these inhibitors doing? Basically, they are going to inhibit
[00:01:35.056] either the anodic reaction or they'll inhibit the cathodic reaction and therefore they will help us to control corrosion. But the only
[00:01:45.124] Problem with this corrosion inhibitor is that it can be used only in a confined environment. That can be understood because the concept is we are adding some substance into the corrosive environment. So obviously we cannot use corrosion inhibitors in an open environment. It has to be an enclosed
[00:02:02.896] environment so we say it is used only in confined environment. Now the
[00:02:09.424] Action of the corrosion inhibitor obviously will depend on the article which has to be protected as well as the corrosive environment. So you know it there is no general corrosion inhibitor which can be used in all the cases. We need to study the specific case.
[00:02:27.088] what is the nature of the metal, what is the corrosive environment, and then decide what corrosion inhibitor would be suitable to protect that article from corrosion.
[00:02:37.472] Now since we have two sets of reactions, one happening at the anode and the other is happening at the cathode, we will have two types of corrosion inhibitors, anodic inhibitors and cathodic inhibitors.
[00:02:50.468] Let us understand what is an anodic inhibitor. Now at the anode, what is the reaction? We know metal is getting oxidized forming mn plus plus n electron n electrons.
